findings.title: New SCAN.ARGS_FORM enforces a narrower exemption set than the standing RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM promise
locations: policy/RULES.toml RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM check field (new, this diff)
findings.before: RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM has stood since before this diff (untouched by it) reading: "Exempt: a thin allocating wrapper, which documents no arguments at all; an internal `_`-prefixed helper, which documents its arguments in whatever form reads best; and a single element-type keyword bound in one prose clause." No scan or doctor check enforced this rule at base — a reader could rely on the written exemptions with no machine second-guessing them.
findings.after: This diff adds the rule's first-ever enforcer, SCAN.ARGS_FORM ('new 2026-09-09' per the scans table), whose implementation only recognises two exemptions: `startswith(d.binding, "_")` and `occursin(Reflection.WRAPPER_PHRASE, d.body)` (plus a fields-list skip). Its logic is `wants_bullets = length(pos) + length(kw) >= Reflection.ARGS_THRESHOLD || !isempty(kw)` — ANY keyword argument, including the exact case the rubric calls out ("a single element-type keyword bound in one prose clause"), now forces the bulleted form and is flagged `wrong-args-form` if written in prose.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader of docs-rubric.md — the rubric this package renders into every consumer's CLAUDE.md — is told a single element-type keyword documented in running prose is fine. The newly-built scan disagrees and will flag it in every fleet package the moment `check-docs` runs there, with no ledger entry or rubric footnote explaining the gap. Because the scan is triage tier it won't fail a round outright, but it manufactures a finding a reviewer must then dismiss every time the documented exemption is exercised, and a first-time reader has no way to know the written rule and the running tool disagree.
findings.description: The diff builds the first mechanical enforcer for a rule whose text (left untouched, so it is the honest baseline of what the package promises) names three exemptions; the enforcer implements only two of them. This is exactly the shape of a check shipped without checking it against its own rule's stated exceptions — the kind of gap RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK's self-application sweep (also new in this diff) was meant to surface, but the sweep only verifies that a `check` field exists, not that the check matches the rule's text.
findings.evidence: policy/docs-rubric.md: "a single element-type keyword bound in one prose clause" (exempt) vs src/Scans/args_form.jl: "wants_bullets = length(pos) + length(kw) >= Reflection.ARGS_THRESHOLD || !isempty(kw)" with no exemption path for a lone keyword.
